original_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: the Integral Conjecture, asking whether for an open set B ⊂ R^n and a positive measure σ on B for which every polynomial is σ-integrable, the subspace M_B(σ) = {f ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] | ∫_B f(z) dσ(z) = 0} is a Mathieu subspace of C[z_1,…,z_n].
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the core object: the zero-integral subspace of a complex polynomial algebra, and it asks exactly the Mathieu-subspace question that the paper isolates as its Integral Conjecture. It also captures the eventual-vanishing conclusion in the Mathieu condition and keeps the problem in the commutative polynomial setting over C.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is over the complex polynomial algebra C[z] = C[z_1,…,z_n], not an arbitrary commutative R-algebra A.
The domain of integration in the paper is an arbitrary open subset B of R^n, not an unspecified C_n.
The measure is an arbitrary positive measure σ on B, not necessarily Lebesgue measure dx.
A standing hypothesis is that every polynomial in C[z_1,…,z_n] is integrable over B with respect to σ.
The paper denotes the zero-integral space as a C-subspace of C[z], so the ambient field and linearity are over C.
The variable set and dimension n should be stated explicitly: z = (z_1,…,z_n), n ≥ 1.
To be paper-faithful, the Mathieu-subspace condition should be stated in the paper’s official form: if f^m ∈ M for all m ≥ 1, then g f^m ∈ M for all sufficiently large m, for every g.
The phrase “for all sufficiently large m” should be made explicit as: there exists N such that the statement holds for all m ≥ N.
If one keeps the integral formulation rather than the abstract Mathieu-subspace definition, one should spell out that f^m ∈ M_B(σ) means ∫_B f(z)^m dσ(z) = 0.
The draft omits the paper’s nearby equivalent reformulation from Proposition 1.2, which expresses the conjecture directly in terms of vanishing moments ∫_B f^m dσ and ∫_B f^m g dσ.
refined_question: Let n ≥ 1, let B be an open subset of R^n, and let σ be a positive measure on B such that ∫_B h(z) dσ(z) is finite for every polynomial h ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n]. Define M_B(σ) := {f ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] | ∫_B f(z) dσ(z) = 0}. Is M_B(σ) a Mathieu subspace of the C-algebra C[z_1,…,z_n]? Equivalently, whenever f ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] satisfies ∫_B f(z)^m dσ(z) = 0 for all m ≥ 1, must it follow that for every g ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] there exists N such that ∫_B f(z)^m g(z) dσ(z) = 0 for all m ≥ N?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (Proposition 1.2), for every f, g ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n], if ∫_B f(z)^m dσ(z) = 0 for all m ≥ 1, then ∫_B f(z)^m g(z) dσ(z) = 0 for all sufficiently large m.
justification: Your draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s Integral Conjecture from the introduction: it asks whether the kernel of the integration functional is a Mathieu subspace. What is already faithful is the zero-integral subspace and the Mathieu-subspace conclusion. What needs sharpening is the exact ambient algebra (C[z_1,…,z_n]), the general domain/measure pair (open B ⊂ R^n with positive σ), the integrability hypothesis for all polynomials, and the official quantifiers in the Mathieu condition. Proposition 1.2 gives the stand-alone integral reformulation, so the refined question above is both self-contained and as close as possible to the paper’s own statement.
